scope: Bounded read-only qmsg fixture/API review; no qmsg or qmesh edits and no additional workload executions by this reviewer

known_findings_reread_as_addressed.finding: Latest source initiates only server close, makes healthy peer progress while pumping the victim, requires peer_closed via the public outcome path, and waits for the client session to disappear. The accepted request deadline is5s and the overall owner clock remains bounded.
Unexpected owned final takeOutcome events are now deinitialized before returning the duplicate-outcome fixture error.

remaining_review_notes.classification: Fixture qualification caveat; no runtime defect demonstrated
remaining_review_notes.finding: The current role-rejection counter accepts any closing/absent third-session status. Initial valid clients and a later reconnect prove general usability, but do not directly exclude third-session or TLS admission failure at the same two-live-client load. A matched valid extra-session readiness control would strengthen the claim. SessionStatus exposes no auth-specific close reason.

The observed peak walks IDs received through connected events; connecting/rejected half-open sessions are not included. max_sessions4 still enforces the actual configured cap. Label the value as observed connected sessions when interpreting results.

Retained late-reply attempts correctly allow immediate public API refusal or later client suppression. Two attempts do not by themselves establish that delayed response bytes reached the wire; do not present this as a controlled late-datagram replay.

positive_observations: Owner time is monotonic and shared across explicit pumps; relative request deadlines use the latest owner tick. GOAWAY advances the public owner clock and the next step reads a later clock value.

All normal server/client/extra event batches and explicit takeOutcome results are deinitialized, including early errors. Deferred replies retain their handles, and the four retained handles must all be released before success.

The exact Unauthorized error reply and server-side prohibition on denied-request delivery make subject authorization denial nonvacuous. The authenticator is explicitly a deterministic capability fixture, not a token-cryptography test.

Two accepted requests fill inflight admission; cancellation retains a completion reservation until takeOutcome consumes it. Ordinary event capacity0 is forced while all15 accepted operations must still produce exactly one terminal result.
Ledger lookup keys opaque request ID and actor separately; colliding wire IDs use actor-specific byte patterns to detect wrong-route replies.
The admitted graceful request is held before GOAWAY; the peer must receive exact code/reason, refuse new requests, complete the retained reply, and close while the other client keeps progressing.
The opt-in public-fault-test and selected parent checkpoint execute the workload directly; the guarded CLI exit alone is not sufficient acceptance evidence.
